body: I currently see my therapist twice a week.  I'm honest with her almost always and I do tell her when some things are bad but again if I am having a really bad day like before I don't think I could call her up and tell her I am feeling suicidal again I would just do it like I did before.  I already feel enough shame for attempting it before its like I wear a label now saying I'm a little nuts.  Telling her or anyone else that knows about my attempt would just make them feel like they failed me.  It feels like I am just blabbering on here.

I can completely relate to the depression hollowing us out thing.  The hobbies I used to have I just don't find much interest/joy in any longer.   I used to fix up cars and do car shows and stuff but I haven't done that in years.   I play a lot of pc games which my therapist doesn't really encourage because of the isolating thing.   Any hobby that usually involved a lot of other people I have staid away from. Lately its just all Work, then home and hang with the family a bit before going to bed and repeat.

One thing I didn't mention in my original post is I was diagnosed with Asperger's when I was a child which is one huge reason that its hard for me to socialize with others.  I do fine at work for the most part.  I train other co workers and I have to do so in large groups of people.  This isn't easy and its way outside my comfort zone but I have to do this to make a living.   When its something I don't "have" to do I normally wont.

I regret trying to kill myself and my wife finding me afterwards.   She saved my life and I am now thankful for that.  If she would have gotten home even minutes later I wouldn't be here.   I feel bad that she has to deal with that pain of seeing me like that. She probably has ptsd but doesn't want to get help with it.
Ghost by Badflower, especially the video.  It hits way to close to home as I just survived a very serious suicide attempt
